deep.reconstruction:
There is no computation or derivation on this page. It holds philosophical and historical notes on the foundations of arithmetic, around 1891.

(a) Kronecker's programme (continued from the previous page). Kronecker does not aim to build mathematics logically or systematically. He takes methods that have given correct results in higher mathematics and applies them to the foundations of number theory. Hilbert lists the key notions: 'Begriff der Aequivalenz und Invariante. Summe gleich Invariante.' This summarises Kronecker's 1887 essay 'Über den Zahlbegriff' and his 1891 course on the concept of number. There, arithmetic objects are treated through equivalence of systems, and e.g. the sum or cardinal number is the invariant of a class of equivalent (bijectively correspondent, or congruent) systems. In modern terms: a number is an invariant of an equivalence relation, i.e. a function constant on equivalence classes, and addition is defined through invariants of unions of systems (my gloss).

(b) Polemical judgement. 'Kronecker's mathematics is partly dreary, external formula-mongering, and partly vague sentimental mush (Gefühlsduselei).'

(c) Anecdote. Brix wrote a dissertation on the concept of number. Hilbert records that Kronecker remarked in connection with it that 'Weierstrass would be nothing'. The source is a report by Ernst Meyer, who attended Kronecker's lecture course on the concept of number. That course is presumably Kronecker's last course, summer semester 1891, 'Über den Begriff der Zahl in der Mathematik'.

(d) Hilbert's own position on the existence of irrational numbers. The dispute over their existence is pointless if one defines an irrational number as the 'carrier of a law' (Träger eines Gesetzes). That is: if I am later given a law (e.g. a rule generating a Cauchy sequence or a Dedekind cut), I can make all my general assertions about it.

The invention of irrational numbers is thus as legitimate, and of the same value, as the invention of the differential calculus. Hilbert first wrote 'Gleichung', struck it, and continues 'Rechnung' on the next page. In both cases, the repeatedly recurring inferences are performed in advance, once, in general form.

The next page develops this into an interpretation of universal statements as conditionals about objects 'encountered later', with examples from Minkowski and power series. It is an early statement of Hilbert's anti-Kroneckerian, implicitly definitional view of mathematical existence.

results.what: Summary of Kronecker's foundational approach: numbers and sums as invariants of equivalence classes of systems
results.modern_name: Number as invariant of an equivalence relation (cardinality via bijection, abstraction principle)
results.usually_credited_to: Kronecker, 'Über den Zahlbegriff' (1887) and lectures of 1891; related ideas from Frege, Cantor and Dedekind

results.what: Irrational number defined as 'carrier of a law'; existence disputes declared void; general theorems read as anticipations of later instances, by analogy with the calculus
results.modern_name: Early Hilbertian implicit-definition / consistency view of mathematical existence (anti-Kronecker stance)
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's views as known from later published work (Über den Zahlbegriff 1900, Paris 1900, Heidelberg 1904); also in the literature on his notebooks (Rowe, Corry, Sieg)

results.what: Anecdote about Kronecker, Brix's dissertation, and the remark that 'Weierstrass would be nothing', via Ernst Meyer
results.modern_name: Historical testimony on the Kronecker–Weierstrass conflict
results.usually_credited_to: Not applicable; historical anecdote. Brix's thesis is 'Der mathematische Zahlbegriff und seine Entwicklungsformen' (Leipzig, c. 1889)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is philosophical and anecdotal, not technical. Hilbert's hostility to Kronecker and his view of existence are well known, and these notebook passages from around 1891 (with the Study letter) have been used by historians. The specific 'Träger eines Gesetzes' formulation and the Brix/Meyer anecdote are mildly interesting unpublished details, but they contain no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'ist als zu einem Theil' could also be read 'ist also zu einem Theil'; the image is ambiguous.
After 'Zahlbegriff' the marks read as 'u[?]' are more likely quotation or punctuation marks, not 'u'. Read: 'eine Dissertation über den "Zahlbegriff" gemacht, zu welchem Kronecker geäussert hat'.
'Difinition' is as written in the manuscript (a slip for 'Definition').
The final struck word is 'Gleichung', and the sentence continues with 'Rechnung' on the next page (Differentialrechnung).
